territorial_scope.description: Applies to AI science and technology, industrial, application and governance activities within the administrative region of Shanghai Municipality.

summary.short: Shanghai municipal regulation, in force from 1 October 2022, promoting the AI industry through compute and data measures, R&D and industrial support, and public-sector and sectoral application. It sets prohibitions on certain algorithmic practices for AI providers and employers, and biometric safeguards.
summary.long: The Regulations apply within the municipality's administrative region (Art. 3) and come into force on 1 October 2022 (Art. 72). They assign roles to municipal and district governments and create an AI strategy advisory committee and an AI ethics expert committee (Arts. 5-7, 66). They provide for public compute and data-opening measures, R&D and industrial support, special funds, additional deductions for AI R&D costs, and talent policies (Arts. 13-34). Application provisions cover government procurement, demonstration lists and sector uses such as manufacturing, finance, medicine and transport (Arts. 46-63). Article 65 provides checklist-style compliance review for high-risk AI products and services, disclosure in advance and after-the-fact control for lower-risk ones, and sandbox regulation. Article 67 prohibits products that endanger security or privacy, discrimination on listed grounds, and algorithmic price discrimination or consumption fraud. Article 68 requires biometric service providers to adopt secure technical safeguards, and Article 69 regulates employers' use of AI in labor discipline, scheduling and recruitment or promotion decisions. Article 67 states no penalty; Article 65 allows a list of non-administrative penalties for minor violations to be formulated.

notes: Text as provided (adopted version, Shanghai Municipality; adoption date not stated in the text). The document has no Chapter 6 heading (Chapter 5 is followed by Chapter 7), though article numbering is continuous from 1 to 72. No penalty or enforcement article appears; Article 65 only refers to a list of non-administrative penalties for minor violations to be formulated by relevant departments. Article 65 uses the categories 'high-risk' and 'low- and medium-risk' AI products without defining them, and leaves the specific measures to the Municipal People's Government. Article 72 sets entry into force on October 1, 2022. target_instrument_id is left as an empty string because the schema requires a string, and the targets are not registry instruments.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff changing legal treatment was found. Article 65 sorts AI products and services into high-risk and low/medium-risk categories without numeric criteria, and says the specific measures will be formulated separately by the Municipal People's Government. SMEs (Art. 13) and special funds (Art. 31) are referenced without numbers. Article 72 gives an effective date (October 1, 2022), which is not a threshold.
